Understand that integers can be divided, provided that the divisor is not zero, and every quotient of integers (with non-zero divisor) is a rational number. If p and q are integers, then -( p / q ) = (- p )/ q = p /(- q ). Interpret quotients of rational numbers by describing real- world contexts.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Properties of Rational Multiplication/Div
nodes.statement: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division and of fractions to multiply and divide rational numbers. Apply properties of operations as strategies to multiply and divide rational numbers.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Converting Rational Numbers to Decimals
nodes.statement: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division and of fractions to multiply and divide rational numbers. Convert a rational number to a decimal using long division; know that the decimal form of a rational number terminates in 0s or eventually repeats.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Rational Numbers Word Problems
nodes.statement: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving the four operations with rational numbers. 1
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Computing Unit Rates with Fractions
nodes.statement: Compute unit rates associated with ratios of fractions, including ratios of lengths, areas and other quantities measured in like or different units. For example, if a person walks 1/2 mile in each 1/ 4 hour, compute the unit rate as the complex fraction 1/2 / 1/ 4 miles per hour, equivalently 2 miles per hour.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Deciding Proportional Relationships
nodes.statement: Recognize and represent proportional relationships between quantities. Decide whether two quantities are in a proportional relationship,
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Identifying Constant of Proportionality
nodes.statement: Recognize and represent proportional relationships between quantities. Identify the constant of proportionality (unit rate) in tables, graphs, equations, diagrams, and verbal descriptions of proportional relationships.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Representing Proportional Relations by Equations
nodes.statement: Recognize and represent proportional relationships between quantities. Represent proportional relationships by equations. For example, if total cost t is proportional to the number n of items purchased at a constant price p, the relationship between the total cost and the number of items can be expressed as t = pn .
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Explaining Proportional Coordinates (1, r)
nodes.statement: Recognize and represent proportional relationships between quantities. Explain what a point (x, y) on the graph of a proportional relationship means in terms of the situation, with special attention to the points (0, 0) and (1, r) where r is the unit rate.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Recognize and represent proportional relationships
nodes.statement: Recognize and represent proportional relationships between quantities. g., by testing for equivalent ratios in a table or graphing on a coordinate plane and observing whether the graph is a straight line through the origin.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Multi-Step Ratio and Percent Problems
nodes.statement: Use proportional relationships to solve multistep ratio and percent problems. Examples: simple interest, tax, markups and markdowns, gratuities and commissions, fees, percent increase and decrease, percent error.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Analyze proportional relationships and use
nodes.statement: Analyze proportional relationships and use them to solve real-world and mathematical problems.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Understanding Random Sampling
nodes.statement: Understand that statistics can be used to gain information about a population by examining a sample of the population; generalizations about a population from a sample are valid only if the sample is representative of that population. Understand that random sampling tends to produce representative samples and support valid inferences.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Drawing Inferences from Random Samples
nodes.statement: Use data from a random sample to draw inferences about a population with an unknown characteristic of interest. Generate multiple samples (or simulated samples) of the same size to gauge the variation in estimates or predictions. For example, estimate the mean word length in a book by randomly sampling words from the book; predict the winner of a school election based on randomly sampled survey data. Gauge how far off the estimate or prediction might be. Draw informal comparative inferences about two populations.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Comparing Data Distributions of Two Populations
nodes.statement: Informally assess the degree of visual overlap of two numerical data distributions with similar variabilities, measuring the difference between the centers by expressing it as a multiple of a measure of variability. For example, the mean height of players on the basketball team is 10 cm greater than the mean height of players on the soccer team, about twice the variability (mean absolute deviation) on either team; on a dot plot, the separation between the two distributions of heights is noticeable.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Measures of Center and Variability Comparisons
nodes.statement: Use measures of center and measures of variability for numerical data from random samples to draw informal comparative inferences about two populations. For example, decide whether the words in a chapter of a seventh-grade science book are generally longer than the words in a chapter of a fourth-grade science book. Investigate chance processes and develop, use, and evaluate probability models.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Probability of Chance Events (0 to 1)
nodes.statement: Understand that the probability of a chance event is a number between 0 and 1 that expresses the likelihood of the event occurring. Larger numbers indicate greater likelihood. A probability near 0 indicates an unlikely event, a probability around 1/2 indicates an event that is neither unlikely nor likely, and a probability near 1 indicates a likely event.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Relative Frequency Approximations
nodes.statement: Approximate the probability of a chance event by collecting data on the chance process that produces it and observing its long-run relative frequency, and predict the approximate relative frequency given the probability. For example, when rolling a number cube 600 times, predict that a 3 or 6 would be rolled roughly 200 times, but probably not exactly 200 times.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Developing Uniform Probability Models
nodes.statement: Develop a probability model and use it to find probabilities of events. Compare probabilities from a model to observed frequencies; if the agreement is not good, explain possible sources of the discrepancy. Develop a uniform probability model by assigning equal probability to all outcomes, and use the model to determine probabilities of events. For example, if a student is selected at random from a class, find the probability that Jane will be selected and the probability that a girl will be selected.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Developing Observed Frequency Probability Models
nodes.statement: Develop a probability model and use it to find probabilities of events. Compare probabilities from a model to observed frequencies; if the agreement is not good, explain possible sources of the discrepancy. Develop a probability model (which may not be uniform) by observing frequencies in data generated from a chance process. For example, find the approximate probability that a spinning penny will land heads up or that a tossed paper cup will land open-end down. Do the outcomes for the spinning penny appear to be equally likely based on the observed frequencies?
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Probability of Compound Events
nodes.statement: Find probabilities of compound events using organized lists, tables, tree diagrams, and simulation. Understand that, just as with simple events, the probability of a compound event is the fraction of outcomes in the sample space for which the compound event occurs.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Representing Sample Spaces of Compound Events
nodes.statement: Find probabilities of compound events using organized lists, tables, tree diagrams, and simulation. Represent sample spaces for compound events using methods such as organized lists, tables and tree diagrams. For an event described in everyday language (e.g., "rolling double sixes"), identify the outcomes in the sample space which compose the event.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Simulations of Compound Events
nodes.statement: Find probabilities of compound events using organized lists, tables, tree diagrams, and simulation. Design and use a simulation to generate frequencies for compound events. For example, use random digits as a simulation tool to approximate the answer to the question: If 40% of donors have type A blood, what is the probability that it will take at least 4 donors to find one with type A blood?
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Properties of Integer Exponents
nodes.statement: Know and apply the properties of integer exponents to generate equivalent numerical expressions. For example, 3 2  × 3 -5 = 3 -3 = 1/3 3 = 1/27.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Square Roots and Cube Roots Solving
nodes.statement: Use square root and cube root symbols to represent solutions to equations of the form x 2 = p and x 3 = p , where p is a positive rational number. Evaluate square roots of small perfect squares and cube roots of small perfect cubes. Know that √2 is irrational.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Powers of Ten and Scientific Notation
nodes.statement: Use numbers expressed in the form of a single digit times an integer power of 10 to estimate very large or very small quantities, and to express how many times as much one is than the other. For example, estimate the population of the United States as 3 × 10 8 and the population of the world as 7 × 10 9 , and determine that the world population is more than 20 times larger.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Operations with Scientific Notation
nodes.statement: Perform operations with numbers expressed in scientific notation, including problems where both decimal and scientific notation are used. Use scientific notation and choose units of appropriate size for measurements of very large or very small quantities (e.g., use millimeters per year for seafloor spreading). Interpret scientific notation that has been generated by technology. Understand the connections between proportional relationships, lines, and linear equations.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Graphing Proportional Relations and Unit Rate
nodes.statement: Graph proportional relationships, interpreting the unit rate as the slope of the graph. Compare two different proportional relationships represented in different ways. For example, compare a distance-time graph to a distance-time equation to determine which of two moving objects has greater speed.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Deriving y = mx and y = mx + b Equations
nodes.statement: Use similar triangles to explain why the slope m is the same between any two distinct points on a non-vertical line in the coordinate plane; derive the equation y = mx for a line through the origin and the equation y = mx + b for a line intercepting the vertical axis at b . Analyze and solve linear equations and pairs of simultaneous linear equations.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Analyzing Linear Equations Solutions (0, 1, inf)
nodes.statement: Solve linear equations in one variable. Give examples of linear equations in one variable with one solution, infinitely many solutions, or no solutions. Show which of these possibilities is the case by successively transforming the given equation into simpler forms, until an equivalent equation of the form x = a , a = a , or a = b results (where a and b are different numbers).
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Solving One-Variable Linear Equations
nodes.statement: Solve linear equations in one variable. Solve linear equations with rational number coefficients, including equations whose solutions require expanding expressions using the distributive property and collecting like terms.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Systems of Linear Equations Intersections
nodes.statement: Analyze and solve pairs of simultaneous linear equations. Understand that solutions to a system of two linear equations in two variables correspond to points of intersection of their graphs, because points of intersection satisfy both equations simultaneously.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Solving Linear Systems Algebraically
nodes.statement: Analyze and solve pairs of simultaneous linear equations. Solve systems of two linear equations in two variables algebraically, and estimate solutions by graphing the equations. Solve simple cases by inspection. For example, 3x + 2y = 5 and 3x + 2y = 6 have no solution because 3x + 2y cannot simultaneously be 5 and 6.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Solving Real-World Linear Systems Problems
nodes.statement: Analyze and solve pairs of simultaneous linear equations. Solve real-world and mathematical problems leading to two linear equations in two variables. For example, given coordinates for two pairs of points, determine whether the line through the first pair of points intersects the line through the second pair.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Definition of Mathematical Functions
nodes.statement: Understand that a function is a rule that assigns to each input exactly one output. The graph of a function is the set of ordered pairs consisting of an input and the corresponding output. 1
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Comparing Linear Functions Properties
nodes.statement: Compare properties of two functions each represented in a different way (algebraically, graphically, numerically in tables, or by verbal descriptions). For example, given a linear function represented by a table of values and a linear function represented by an algebraic expression, determine which function has the greater rate of change.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Linear vs Non-Linear Functions
nodes.statement: Interpret the equation y = mx + b as defining a linear function, whose graph is a straight line; give examples of functions that are not linear. For example, the function A = s 2 giving the area of a square as a function of its side length is not linear because its graph contains the points (1,1), (2,4) and (3,9), which are not on a straight line. Use functions to model relationships between quantities.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Constructing Linear Models of Relations
nodes.statement: Construct a function to model a linear relationship between two quantities. Determine the rate of change and initial value of the function from a description of a relationship or from two ( x , y ) values, including reading these from a table or from a graph. Interpret the rate of change and initial value of a linear function in terms of the situation it models, and in terms of its graph or a table of values.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Qualitatively Describing Functional Behaviors
nodes.statement: Describe qualitatively the functional relationship between two quantities by analyzing a graph (e.g., where the function is increasing or decreasing, linear or nonlinear). Sketch a graph that exhibits the qualitative features of a function that has been described verbally.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Lines Congruence Under Rotations
nodes.statement: Verify experimentally the properties of rotations, reflections, and translations: Lines are taken to lines, and line segments to line segments of the same length.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Angles Congruence Under Rotations
nodes.statement: Verify experimentally the properties of rotations, reflections, and translations: Angles are taken to angles of the same measure.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Parallel Lines Congruence Under Rotations
nodes.statement: Verify experimentally the properties of rotations, reflections, and translations: Parallel lines are taken to parallel lines.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Congruent Figures Transformations Definition
nodes.statement: Understand that a two-dimensional figure is congruent to another if the second can be obtained from the first by a sequence of rotations, reflections, and translations; given two congruent figures, describe a sequence that exhibits the congruence between them. 1 Function notation is not required in Grade 8.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Coordinate Transformations Descriptions
nodes.statement: Describe the effect of dilations, translations, rotations, and reflections on two-dimensional figures using coordinates.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Similar Figures Transformations Definition
nodes.statement: Understand that a two-dimensional figure is similar to another if the second can be obtained from the first by a sequence of rotations, reflections, translations, and dilations; given two similar two- dimensional figures, describe a sequence that exhibits the similarity between them.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Angle Sum and Exterior Angle of Triangles
nodes.statement: Use informal arguments to establish facts about the angle sum and exterior angle of triangles, about the angles created when parallel lines are cut by a transversal, and the angle-angle criterion for similarity of triangles. For example, arrange three copies of the same triangle so that the sum of the three angles appears to form a line, and give an argument in terms of transversals why this is so. Understand and apply the Pythagorean Theorem.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Pythagorean Theorem Proof Concepts
nodes.statement: Explain a proof of the Pythagorean Theorem and its converse.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Applying Pythagorean Theorem in 2D & 3D
nodes.statement: Apply the Pythagorean Theorem to determine unknown side lengths in right triangles in real-world and mathematical problems in two and three dimensions.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Pythagorean Distance Formula on Coordinate Plane
nodes.statement: Apply the Pythagorean Theorem to find the distance between two points in a coordinate system. Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving volume of cylinders, cones, and spheres.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Volume of Cones, Cylinders, Spheres
nodes.statement: Know the formulas for the volumes of cones, cylinders, and spheres and use them to solve real-world and mathematical problems.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Rational vs Irrational Numbers
nodes.statement: Know that numbers that are not rational are called irrational. Understand informally that every number has a decimal expansion; for rational numbers show that the decimal expansion repeats eventually, and convert a decimal expansion which repeats eventually into a rational number.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Approximating Irrational Numbers
nodes.statement: Use rational approximations of irrational numbers to compare the size of irrational numbers, locate them approximately on a number line diagram, and estimate the value of expressions (e.g., π 2 ). For example, by truncating the decimal expansion of √2, show that √2 is between 1 and 2, then between 1.4 and 1.5, and explain how to continue on to get better approximations.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Know that there are numbers
nodes.statement: Know that there are numbers that are not rational, and approximate them by rational numbers.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Bivariate Association Scatter Plots
nodes.statement: Construct and interpret scatter plots for bivariate measurement data to investigate patterns of association between two quantities. Describe patterns such as clustering, outliers, positive or negative association, linear association, and nonlinear association.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Line of Best Fit Approximations
nodes.statement: Know that straight lines are widely used to model relationships between two quantitative variables. For scatter plots that suggest a linear association, informally fit a straight line, and informally assess the model fit by judging the closeness of the data points to the line.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Linear Fit Equation Analysis
nodes.statement: Use the equation of a linear model to solve problems in the context of bivariate measurement data, interpreting the slope and intercept. For example, in a linear model for a biology experiment, interpret a slope of 1.5 cm/hr as meaning that an additional hour of sunlight each day is associated with an additional 1.5 cm in mature plant height.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Two-Way Frequency Tables for Categorical Data
nodes.statement: Understand that patterns of association can also be seen in bivariate categorical data by displaying frequencies and relative frequencies in a two-way table. Construct and interpret a two-way table summarizing data on two categorical variables collected from the same subjects. Use relative frequencies calculated for rows or columns to describe possible association between the two variables. For example, collect data from students in your class on whether or not they have a curfew on school nights and whether or not they have assigned chores at home. Is there evidence that those who have a curfew also tend to have chores?
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Structure of Atom
nodes.statement: Bohr's model, dual nature of matter and radiation, Heisenberg uncertainty, quantum numbers, shapes of s, p, d orbitals, Aufbau principle, Pauli exclusion, and Hund's rule.
nodes.subject: Chemistry

nodes.title: Biomolecules & Biological Macromolecules
nodes.statement: Carbohydrates (classification, glucose/fructose structure), proteins (amino acids, peptide bonds, denaturation), nucleic acids (DNA, RNA, chemical composition, double helix structure), enzymes, and vitamins.
nodes.subject: Chemistry

nodes.title: Chemical Bonding & Molecular Structure
nodes.statement: Valence electrons, ionic and covalent bonds, Lewis structures, polar character, VSEPR theory, hybridization (sp, sp2, sp3, dsp2, d2sp3), and Molecular Orbital (MO) theory of homonuclear diatomic molecules.
nodes.subject: Chemistry

nodes.title: Coordination Compounds & CFT
nodes.statement: Ligands, coordination number, Werner's coordination theory, IUPAC nomenclature, isomerism, Valence Bond Theory (VBT), and Crystal Field Theory (CFT) splitting of d-orbitals in octahedral and tetrahedral fields.
nodes.subject: Chemistry

nodes.title: Electrochemistry & Nernst Equation
nodes.statement: Galvanic cells, EMF, Nernst equation, Gibbs energy of cell reaction, electrolytic conductance, specific and molar conductivity, Kohlrausch's law, electrolysis laws, and batteries/fuel cells.
nodes.subject: Chemistry

nodes.title: Chemical & Ionic Equilibrium
nodes.statement: Law of mass action, equilibrium constant (Kp, Kc), Le Chatelier's principle, ionic dissociation, pH, weak/strong electrolytes, buffer solutions, Henderson-Hasselbalch equation, and solubility product (Ksp).
nodes.subject: Chemistry

nodes.title: States of Matter & Gas Laws
nodes.statement: Gas laws (Boyle, Charles, Gay-Lussac, Avogadro), ideal gas equation, Dalton's law of partial pressures, kinetic molecular theory of gases, deviation from ideal behavior, liquefaction of gases, and liquid states properties (viscosity, surface tension).
nodes.subject: Chemistry

nodes.title: Hydrocarbons & Alkanes/Alkenes/Alkynes
nodes.statement: Preparation, physical and chemical properties of alkanes, alkenes (electrophilic addition, Markovnikov's rule), alkynes (acidity, addition), and aromatic hydrocarbons (benzene structure, resonance, electrophilic substitution).
nodes.subject: Chemistry

nodes.title: The d- and f-Block Elements
nodes.statement: Electronic configuration, oxidation states, ionic radii, color, catalytic properties, magnetic properties, interstitial compounds, alloy formation, lanthanoid contraction, and actinoid characteristics.
nodes.subject: Chemistry

nodes.title: Chemical Kinetics & Activation Energy
nodes.statement: Rate of reaction, factors affecting rate, rate law and specific rate constant, integrated rate equations (zero and first-order reactions), half-life, collision theory, activation energy, and the Arrhenius equation.
nodes.subject: Chemistry

nodes.title: Amines & Nitrogen Compounds
nodes.statement: Classification, nomenclature, structure, preparation methods, physical/chemical properties, basicity of aliphatic and aromatic amines, and synthetic utility of diazonium salts.
nodes.subject: Chemistry

nodes.title: Organic Chemistry: Basic Principles & Techniques
nodes.statement: IUPAC nomenclature, isomerism (structural and stereoisomerism), electronic displacement effects (inductive, electromeric, resonance, hyperconjugation), homolytic/heterolytic cleavage, carbocations, carbanions, free radicals, and purification techniques (chromatography, distillation).
nodes.subject: Chemistry

nodes.title: Haloalkanes and Haloarenes
nodes.statement: Nomenclature, C-X bond nature, physical/chemical properties, nucleophilic substitution reactions mechanism (SN1 and SN2 stereochemistry), and environmental effects of organohalogens.
nodes.subject: Chemistry

nodes.title: Alcohols, Phenols & Ethers
nodes.statement: Nomenclature, methods of preparation, physical/chemical properties, acidic nature of phenols, and mechanism of dehydration of alcohols to alkenes/ethers.
nodes.subject: Chemistry

nodes.title: Aldehydes, Ketones & Carboxylic Acids
nodes.statement: Nomenclature, carbonyl group nature, methods of preparation, nucleophilic addition mechanism, reactivity, oxidation/reduction reactions, acidity of carboxylic acids, and effect of substituents on acidity.
nodes.subject: Chemistry

nodes.title: Classification of Elements & Periodicity
nodes.statement: Modern periodic law, s, p, d, f block classifications, and periodic trends (atomic/ionic radii, ionization enthalpy, electron gain enthalpy, electronegativity).
nodes.subject: Chemistry

nodes.title: Symmetry, Group Theory & Spectroscopic Terms
nodes.statement: Symmetry elements and operations, point groups, character tables, great orthogonality theorem, irreducible representations, applications of group theory to molecular vibrations (IR/Raman activity) and chemical bonding, and electronic spectroscopic terms of transition metal complexes.
nodes.subject: Chemistry

nodes.title: Quantum Chemistry & Molecular Orbitals
nodes.statement: Operator algebra, postulates, solvable models (particle-in-a-box, harmonic oscillator, rigid rotor), hydrogen atom wave functions, angular momentum, variational principle, perturbation theory, and Hückel molecular orbital theory for conjugated pi systems.
nodes.subject: Chemistry

nodes.title: Statistical Thermodynamics
nodes.statement: Ensembles, Maxwell-Boltzmann, Fermi-Dirac, and Bose-Einstein statistics, molecular partition functions (translational, rotational, vibrational, electronic), calculation of thermodynamic properties of ideal gases, and statistical formulation of transition state theory.
nodes.subject: Chemistry

nodes.title: Redox Reactions
nodes.statement: Oxidation and reduction concepts, oxidation number, balancing redox equations (electron-transfer and half-reaction methods), and electrochemical cell introductions.
nodes.subject: Chemistry

nodes.title: Solutions & Colligative Properties
nodes.statement: Types of solutions, solubility of gases in liquids (Henry's law), vapor pressure (Raoult's law), ideal and non-ideal solutions, colligative properties (relative lowering of vapor pressure, elevation of boiling point, depression of freezing point, osmotic pressure), van 't Hoff factor.
nodes.subject: Chemistry

nodes.title: Some Basic Concepts of Chemistry
nodes.statement: Law of chemical combinations, mole concept, molar mass, empirical/molecular formulas, stoichiometry, and limiting reactant calculations.
nodes.subject: Chemistry

nodes.title: Chemical Thermodynamics
nodes.statement: System and surroundings, state functions, first law of thermodynamics, enthalpy (H), heat capacity, Hess's law, entropy (S), second law, Gibbs free energy (G), spontaneity, and equilibrium criterion.
nodes.subject: Chemistry

nodes.title: Organometallic Chemistry
nodes.statement: Transition metal organometallic complexes, 18-electron rule, hapticity, ligand types (CO, pi-allyl, cyclopentadienyl), oxidative addition, reductive elimination, migratory insertion, and catalytic cycles (Monsanto acetic acid, Ziegler-Natta, Wilkinson's hydrogenation).
nodes.subject: Chemistry

nodes.title: Advanced Organic Synthesis & Named Reactions
nodes.statement: Retrosynthetic analysis, carbon-carbon bond forming reactions (Aldol, Claisen, Wittig, Diels-Alder, Grignard), modern oxidation/reduction reagents, and selectivity/stereocontrol in organic synthesis.
nodes.subject: Chemistry

nodes.title: Advanced Kinetics & Surface Chemistry
nodes.statement: Complex reaction mechanisms (parallel, consecutive, chain reactions like hydrogen-bromine), transition state theory (activated complex), homogeneous/heterogeneous catalysis, Langmuir adsorption isotherms, and Michaelis-Menten enzyme kinetics.
nodes.subject: Chemistry

nodes.title: Molecular Spectroscopy
nodes.statement: Fundamental principles of UV-Visible, Infrared (IR), Proton and Carbon-13 Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (1H and 13C NMR), and Mass spectrometry for structure elucidation of organic molecules.
nodes.subject: Chemistry

nodes.title: Heuristics & Game Tree Search
nodes.statement: Introduction to AI search techniques, state-space representations, uninformed search, informed heuristic search (A* search), game playing, minimax algorithm, and alpha-beta pruning.
nodes.subject: Computer Science

nodes.title: Deep Learning & Physical AI Architectures
nodes.statement: Deep neural network architectures, Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN/LSTM), attention models, Transformers, self-attention, pre-training, and fine-tuning. Physics-informed neural network (PINN) architectures.
nodes.subject: Computer Science

nodes.title: Perceptrons & Multi-Layer Neural Networks
nodes.statement: Biological vs artificial neurons, single-layer perceptrons, activation functions, multi-layer neural networks, backpropagation optimization, and stochastic gradient descent.
nodes.subject: Computer Science

nodes.title: Statistical Supervised Classifications
nodes.statement: Supervised machine learning algorithms, classification vs regression models, support vector machines (SVM), decision trees, k-nearest neighbors, ensemble models, and model evaluation metrics.
nodes.subject: Computer Science

nodes.title: Unsupervised Clustering & Dimensions
nodes.statement: Unsupervised machine learning algorithms, clustering techniques, centroid k-means, hierarchical clustering, density-based DBSCAN clustering, and linear dimensionality reductions (PCA).
nodes.subject: Computer Science

nodes.title: Asymptotic Analysis & Complexities
nodes.statement: Asymptotic complexity analysis, Big-O, Theta, and Omega notations, sorting algorithms (bubble, insertion, merge, quick, heap), linear/binary search, divide-and-conquer, dynamic programming, and greedy algorithms.
nodes.subject: Computer Science

nodes.title: Graph Search & Shortest Path Algorithms
nodes.statement: Breadth-First Search (BFS), Depth-First Search (DFS), topological sorting, single-source shortest paths (Dijkstra, Bellman-Ford), and minimum spanning trees (Kruskal, Prim).
nodes.subject: Computer Science

nodes.title: Linear Data Structures & Arrays
nodes.statement: Implementation and analysis of linear data structures: static and dynamic arrays, singly and doubly linked lists, stacks, queues, double-ended queues, and hash tables.
nodes.subject: Computer Science

nodes.title: Tree, Graph & Heap Structures
nodes.statement: Hierarchical data structures, binary trees, binary search trees (BST), balanced BSTs (AVL, Red-Black), heaps, and graph data structures (adjacency matrices and lists).
nodes.subject: Computer Science

nodes.title: Foundational Computational Programming
nodes.statement: Basic programming constructs, variables, data types, control structures, loops, functions, scope, arrays, recursion, and object-oriented programming.
nodes.subject: Computer Science

nodes.title: Digital Signal Processing
nodes.statement: Discrete Fourier Transform (DFT), Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) algorithms, linear and circular convolution, digital filter structures (IIR and FIR), finite word-length effects, and multirate DSP.
nodes.subject: Electronics

nodes.title: Embedded Systems & Microcontrollers
nodes.statement: Microprocessor and microcontroller architectures (ARM Cortex, 8051), memory systems, assembly and embedded C programming, hardware interrupts, timers, and interfacing communication protocols (SPI, I2C, UART, CAN).
nodes.subject: Electronics

nodes.title: VLSI Design & Microelectronics
nodes.statement: Physics and fabrication of CMOS devices, CMOS inverter static/dynamic characteristics, combinational and sequential CMOS logic style design, propagation delay, power dissipation, layout rules, and FPGA synthesis.
nodes.subject: Electronics

nodes.title: Analog Semiconductor Circuits
nodes.statement: Physical modeling and biasing of semiconductor Diodes, Bipolar Junction Transistors (BJTs), and Field-Effect Transistors (MOSFETs); small-signal equivalent circuits, differential and operational amplifiers (op-amps) feedback circuits, and active filters.
nodes.subject: Electronics

nodes.title: Network Theory & Circuit Analysis
nodes.statement: Ohm's and Kirchhoff's laws (KCL/KVL), nodal and mesh analysis, network theorems (Thevenin, Norton, Superposition, Maximum Power Transfer), transient response of RC, RL, and RLC circuits, and AC sinusoidal steady-state analysis.
nodes.subject: Electronics

nodes.title: Digital Electronics & Logic Design
nodes.statement: Boolean algebra, logic minimization (Karnaugh maps), combinational circuits (multiplexers, decoders, adders), sequential circuits (latches, flip-flops, registers, counters), and DAC/ADC data conversion.
nodes.subject: Electronics

nodes.title: Signals & Systems
nodes.statement: Continuous and discrete-time signals, Linear Time-Invariant (LTI) systems, convolution, Fourier series, Fourier transforms, Laplace transforms, and Z-transforms.
nodes.subject: Electronics

nodes.title: Counting to 100
nodes.statement: Count to 100 by ones and by tens.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Forward Counting
nodes.statement: Count forward beginning from a given number within the known sequence (instead of having to begin at 1).
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Writing Numbers 0-20
nodes.statement: Write numbers from 0 to 20. Represent a number of objects with a written numeral 0-20 (with 0 representing a count of no objects). Count to tell the number of objects.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: One-to-One Correspondence
nodes.statement: Understand the relationship between numbers and quantities; connect counting to cardinality. When counting objects, say the number names in the standard order, pairing each object with one and only one number name and each number name with one and only one object.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Cardinality Principle
nodes.statement: Understand the relationship between numbers and quantities; connect counting to cardinality. Understand that the last number name said tells the number of objects counted. The number of objects is the same regardless of their arrangement or the order in which they were counted.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Successive Number Addition
nodes.statement: Understand the relationship between numbers and quantities; connect counting to cardinality. Understand that each successive number name refers to a quantity that is one larger.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Counting Objects up to 20
nodes.statement: Count to answer "how many?" questions about as many as 20 things arranged in a line, a rectangular array, or a circle, or as many as 10 things in a scattered configuration; given a number from 1-20, count out that many objects. Compare numbers.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Comparing Sets by Counting
nodes.statement: Identify whether the number of objects in one group is greater than, less than, or equal to the number of objects in another group, e.g., by using matching and counting strategies. 1
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Comparing Two Written Numbers
nodes.statement: Compare two numbers between 1 and 10 presented as written numerals.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Describing Spatial Positions
nodes.statement: Describe objects in the environment using names of shapes, and describe the relative positions of these objects using terms such as above, below, beside, in front of, behind, and next to.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Naming Shapes (2D & 3D)
nodes.statement: Correctly name shapes regardless of their orientations or overall size.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Identifying 2D vs 3D Shapes
nodes.statement: Identify shapes as two-dimensional (lying in a plane, "flat") or three- dimensional ("solid"). Analyze, compare, create, and compose shapes.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Analyzing & Comparing Shapes
nodes.statement: Analyze and compare two- and three-dimensional shapes, in different sizes and orientations, using informal language to describe their similarities, differences, parts (e.g., number of sides and vertices/"corners") and other attributes (e.g., having sides of equal length).
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Building and Drawing Shapes
nodes.statement: Model shapes in the world by building shapes from components (e.g., sticks and clay balls) and drawing shapes.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Composing Simple Shapes
nodes.statement: Compose simple shapes to form larger shapes. For example, "Can you join these two triangles with full sides touching to make a rectangle?" 3 Limit category counts to be less than or equal to 10.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Describing Measurable Attributes
nodes.statement: Describe measurable attributes of objects, such as length or weight. Describe several measurable attributes of a single object.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Comparing Measurable Attributes
nodes.statement: Directly compare two objects with a measurable attribute in common, to see which object has "more of"/"less of" the attribute, and describe the difference. For example, directly compare the heights of two children and describe one child as taller/shorter. Classify objects and count the number of objects in each category.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Classifying and Counting Objects
nodes.statement: Classify objects into given categories; count the numbers of objects in each category and sort the categories by count. 3
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Place Value Foundations (11-19)
nodes.statement: Compose and decompose numbers from 11 to 19 into ten ones and some further ones, e.g., by using objects or drawings, and record each composition or decomposition by a drawing or equation (e.g., 18 = 10 + 8); understand that these numbers are composed of ten ones and one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine ones.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Modeling Addition & Subtraction
nodes.statement: Represent addition and subtraction with objects, fingers, mental images, drawings 2 , sounds (e.g., claps), acting out situations, verbal explanations, expressions, or equations.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Addition & Subtraction Word Problems
nodes.statement: Solve addition and subtraction word problems, and add and subtract within 10, e.g., by using objects or drawings to represent the problem.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Decomposing Numbers under 10
nodes.statement: Decompose numbers less than or equal to 10 into pairs in more than one way, e.g., by using objects or drawings, and record each decomposition by a drawing or equation (e.g., 5 = 2 + 3 and 5 = 4 + 1).
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Making Tens Pairs
nodes.statement: For any number from 1 to 9, find the number that makes 10 when added to the given number, e.g., by using objects or drawings, and record the answer with a drawing or equation.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Fluency in Addition & Subtraction
nodes.statement: Fluently add and subtract within 5. (This applies wherever drawings are mentioned in the Standards.)
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Rings Factorization (UFD, PID, ED)
nodes.statement: Polynomial rings over fields, unique factorization domains (UFD), principal ideal domains (PID), Euclidean domains (ED), and irreducibility criteria.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Real Numbers & Euclid Division
nodes.statement: Euclid's division lemma, Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic, decimal expansions of rational numbers.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Quadratic Equations & Roots
nodes.statement: Quadratic equations, factorization, completing the square, quadratic formula, discriminant and nature of roots.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Galois Field Extensions
nodes.statement: Field extensions, algebraic extensions, splitting fields, normal and separable extensions, Galois groups, and solvability of polynomial equations.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Groups & Lagrange's Theorem
nodes.statement: Groups, subgroups, cyclic groups, cosets, Lagrange's theorem and its algebraic properties.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Quotient Groups & Isomorphisms
nodes.statement: Normal subgroups, quotient groups, group homomorphisms, kernel, First, Second, and Third Isomorphism Theorems.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Algebraic Identities
nodes.statement: Standard algebraic identities and their applications in factorization of polynomials.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Linear Equations in Two Variables
nodes.statement: Linear equations in two variables, standard form ax + by + c = 0, graphing linear equations in 2D.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Linear Systems in 2D
nodes.statement: Pair of linear equations in two variables, graphical method of solution, algebraic methods (substitution, elimination, cross-multiplication).
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Polynomial Algebra
nodes.statement: Polynomials in one variable, coefficients, terms, zeros of a polynomial, degree of a polynomial.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Polynomial Zeros & Coefficients
nodes.statement: Geometrical meaning of zeros of a polynomial, relationship between zeros and coefficients of quadratic polynomials.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Real Number System
nodes.statement: Review of rational numbers, introduction to irrational numbers, real numbers representation on number line.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Ideals & Commutative Rings
nodes.statement: Rings, subrings, ideals, quotient rings, ring homomorphisms, integral domains, fields, characteristic of a ring.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Group Actions & Sylow's Theorems
nodes.statement: Group actions, conjugacy classes, class equation, Sylow's three theorems, symmetric/alternating group structures.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Limits & Uniform Continuity
nodes.statement: Epsilon-delta limits, pointwise continuity, Heine-Borel theorem in R, uniform continuity on intervals, Intermediate Value Theorem, and Darboux's theorem.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Uniform Convergence of Functions
nodes.statement: Sequences and series of functions, pointwise vs uniform convergence, Weierstrass M-test, and uniform convergence integrations and differentiations.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Real Series Convergence Tests
nodes.statement: Infinite series of real numbers, absolute and conditional convergence, comparison test, ratio test, root test, integral test, Leibniz's alternating series test.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Lebesgue Integral & Convergence
nodes.statement: Lebesgue integral of simple and non-negative functions, Monotone Convergence Theorem, Fatou's Lemma, and the Dominated Convergence Theorem.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Lebesgue Outer Measure
nodes.statement: Lebesgue outer measure, outer regularity, Sigma-algebra of measurable sets, Carathéodory's measurability criterion, and Borel sets.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: L^p Normed Spaces
nodes.statement: L^p spaces of measurable functions, norm definitions, Hölder's and Minkowski's inequalities, and completeness proofs.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Lebesgue Measurable Functions
nodes.statement: Measurable functions, pointwise limits, approximations, and Egorov's and Lusin's structural theorems.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Metric Spaces Foundations
nodes.statement: Definition of metric spaces, open and closed sets, limit points, interior/closure, completeness, and Banach contraction mapping theorem.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Riemann Integration Theory
nodes.statement: Darboux upper and lower sums, Riemann sums, integrability criteria, and the mathematical proof of the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Real Sequences & Cauchy Limits
nodes.statement: Sequences of real numbers, bounded and monotonic sequences, convergence, subsequence, Cauchy sequences, completeness of the real line.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: General Topology Spaces
nodes.statement: Topological spaces definition, bases, subbases, continuous maps, homeomorphisms, Hausdorff spaces, compactness, and connectedness.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Binomial Coefficients Identities
nodes.statement: Identities of binomial coefficients, summation equations, binomial expansion of rational, fractional, and negative indices.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Binomial Theorem Expansion
nodes.statement: Expansion of (x+y)^n, Pascal's triangle coefficients, general term, middle term, numerically greatest term calculations.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Continuity of Functions
nodes.statement: Continuity checks on real functions, left and right continuity, Intermediate Value Theorem.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Tangent and Normal Curves
nodes.statement: Rate of change of quantities, tangent and normal line algebraic equations on curves, monotonic (increasing/decreasing) conditions.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Derivatives & Chain Rule
nodes.statement: Derivative formulas, Power rule, Product rule, Quotient rule, Chain rule, derivatives of trig/exponential functions.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Rigor of Differentiability
nodes.statement: Rigor of differentiability, left-hand and right-hand derivative matching, relation to continuity.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Gradients & Tangent Planes
nodes.statement: Gradient vectors, directional derivatives, tangent planes to level surfaces, normal lines, and coordinate gradient properties.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Implicit & Log Differentiation
nodes.statement: Differentiation of implicit equations, parametric curves differentiation, logarithmic differentiation, second-order derivatives.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Jacobian Determinants
nodes.statement: Jacobian matrices and determinants, transformation of coordinates for multivariable integrations, and area/volume scaling factors.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Lagrange Multipliers Optimization
nodes.statement: Constrained optimization of multivariable systems, Lagrange multipliers with single and multiple constraints.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Limits of Functions
nodes.statement: Limits of functions, left and right limits, algebraic limit laws, squeeze theorem, trigonometric limits.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Mean Value Theorems
nodes.statement: Proving and applying Rolle's Theorem and Lagrange's Mean Value Theorem (LMVT) with geometric interpretations.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Multiple Integrals & Fubini
nodes.statement: Double and triple integrals over general regions, Fubini's theorem, and changing coordinates to polar, cylindrical and spherical systems.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Critical Points & Max/Min
nodes.statement: Critical points, local/global maxima and minima, First/Second derivative tests, solving applied geometric optimization models.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Multivariable Partial Derivatives
nodes.statement: Multivariable functions, limits, continuity, partial derivatives, and higher-order mixed derivatives, and the multivariable chain rule.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Advanced Combinatorics
nodes.statement: Circular permutations, identical items selections, derangements, partitions and division of distinct objects into groups.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Fundamental Counting Principles
nodes.statement: Fundamental principle of counting, addition/multiplication rules, factorials.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Selections & Arrangements
nodes.statement: Arrangements vs selections, permutation formula nPr, combination formula nCr, standard combinatorial proofs.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Complex Number Algebra
nodes.statement: Complex algebra as ordered pairs, form a+ib, conjugate, modulus, and division equations.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Analytic Functions & Conformal Mappings
nodes.statement: Cauchy-Riemann equations, analyticity, harmonic functions, harmonic conjugates, and conformal mapping properties.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Complex Functions & Limits
nodes.statement: Complex algebra review, polar form, complex functions of a complex variable, limits, continuity, differentiability.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Complex Number Geometry
nodes.statement: Argand coordinate geometry, polar representation, complex triangle inequalities, cube roots of unity, geometric rotations.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Complex Integration & Cauchy Formula
nodes.statement: Line integrals in complex plane, Cauchy's Integral Theorem, Cauchy's Integral Formula, Liouville's theorem, Fundamental Theorem of Algebra.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Complex Laurent Series & Residues
nodes.statement: Complex Taylor and Laurent series, classification of singularities, poles, Cauchy's Residue Theorem, and contour integration of real functions.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Cartesian Coordinate Plane
nodes.statement: Rectangular coordinate systems, 2D distance formula, section formula, slope of line, parallel and perpendicular slopes.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: 3D Coordinate Grid
nodes.statement: 3D Cartesian coordinate axes, coordinates in space, 3D distance and section formulas.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: 3D Lines & Planes Geometry
nodes.statement: Direction cosines and ratios, angle between lines, vector/Cartesian equations of planes and lines, skew lines, shortest distance.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Cartesian Coordinates
nodes.statement: Cartesian plane, coordinates of a point, names and terms associated with coordinate plane, plotting points.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Circle Coordinate Equations
nodes.statement: Standard and general equations of circles, radius, center, diameter endpoints, tangent line formulas.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Conic Focus-Directrix & Polar Forms
nodes.statement: Foci, directrices, vertex definitions, eccentricity parameter e of conics, classification of curves, polar coordinate representations of general conics.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: General Second-Degree Conic Equations
nodes.statement: General second-degree algebraic equations, discriminant classification of conics (ellipse, parabola, hyperbola, circle, pair of lines), coordinate translations, and rotations.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Conic Normal Line Algebra
nodes.statement: Equations of normal lines to parabolas, ellipses, and hyperbolas in standard coordinate forms, co-normal points properties, and geometric intercepts.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Conic Tangent Line Algebra
nodes.statement: Analytical conditions for line-conic tangency, equations of tangent lines to parabolas, ellipses, and hyperbolas in slope, point, and parametric forms.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Standard Ellipse Equations & Auxiliaries
nodes.statement: Standard ellipse equations, major/minor axes, foci, directrices, eccentricity formulas, auxiliary circles, and parametric coordinate representations.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Coordinate Geometry Formulas
nodes.statement: Coordinate distance formula, section formula, and area of triangle coordinate formulas.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Hyperbola Asymptotes & Rectangular Geometry
nodes.statement: Asymptotes of hyperbolas, angle between asymptotes, rectangular hyperbola equations (xy = c^2), and their parametric coordinate geometry properties.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Standard Hyperbola Equations & Conjugates
nodes.statement: Standard hyperbola equations, transverse/conjugate axes, foci, directrices, eccentricity, conjugate hyperbolas, and parametric coordinate systems.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Standard Parabola Equations & Properties
nodes.statement: Standard parabola equations (y^2=4ax, x^2=4ay), focal chords, focal distance, vertex, parameterizations, and geometric properties of axis and directrix.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Straight-Line Equations
nodes.statement: Straight-line equations in standard forms, angle between two lines, concurrency tests, distance from point to line, centroid/circumcenter.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: ODE Order & Degree
nodes.statement: Ordinary differential equations, order, degree, formation of differential equations from families of curves.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Picard-Lindelof Existence
nodes.statement: Existence and uniqueness of IVPs, Picard-Lindelof theorem, Lipschitz continuity, successive approximations.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Higher-Order Linear ODEs
nodes.statement: Linear higher-order ordinary differential equations with constant coefficients, method of undetermined coefficients, variation of parameters, Euler-Cauchy equations.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Planar Autonomous Stability
nodes.statement: Planar autonomous systems, critical points classification, phase portraits, linearization stability, Lyapunov direct stability function.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Power Series ODE Solutions
nodes.statement: Power series solutions of ordinary differential equations around ordinary and regular singular points, Frobenius method, Legendre and Bessel functions.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: First-Order ODE Methods
nodes.statement: Solving first-order differential equations: variable separable method, homogeneous first-order, linear first-order integrating factors.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Extremal Graphs & Network Flows
nodes.statement: Extremal graph theory, Turán's theorem, Ramsey theory, matching theory, Hall's marriage theorem, network flows, Ford-Fulkerson algorithm, max-flow min-cut theorem, and algebraic graph theory (adjacency spectrum).
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Advanced Combinatorics & Recurrences
nodes.statement: Advanced counting techniques, inclusion-exclusion principle, pigeonhole principle, recurrence relations, generating functions, and stars-and-bars distribution problems.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Graph Theory & Trees
nodes.statement: Graphs, paths, cycles, Eulerian and Hamiltonian paths, planar graphs, Euler's formula for planar graphs, graph coloring, chromatic number, trees, spanning trees, and Kruskal's/Dijkstra's algorithms.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Banach Spaces & Continuous Operators
nodes.statement: Normed linear spaces, Banach spaces, continuous linear operators, dual spaces, open mapping theorem, closed graph theorem, and Hahn-Banach theorem.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Hilbert Spaces & Orthonormal Bessel
nodes.statement: Inner product spaces, Hilbert spaces completeness, orthonormal sets, Bessel's inequality, Parseval's identity, and the Riesz representation theorem.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Spectral Theorem of Operators
nodes.statement: Adjoint operators, self-adjoint, normal, and unitary operators on Hilbert spaces, and spectral theorem for compact self-adjoint operators.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Areas Related to Circles
nodes.statement: Area of sectors and segments of a circle, perimeter and area of circle-related combinations of plane figures.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Circles and Chords
nodes.statement: Circles and related terms, angle subtended by a chord, perpendicular from center to chord, cyclic quadrilaterals.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Circle Tangents & Properties
nodes.statement: Tangents to a circle, theorem: tangent is perpendicular to radius at point of contact, lengths of tangents from external point are equal.
nodes.subject: Mathematics

nodes.title: Congruent Triangles Criteria
nodes.statement: Congruence of triangles, SAS, ASA, SSS, RHS congruence rules, properties of triangles.
